notes.title: Dev Diary #6: Game Update
notes.content:
So it's been a while since the last Dev Diary and I thought it'd be a great time to update everyone about what's been going on and share some screenshots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/7648e81f1bd05a75d15602613c01cd6ce928959b.png[/img]

The game is progressing fine and I've mostly been tweaking and optimizing. One big feature that was completed recently is the Battle Simulator.
The simulator spawns random battles with random heroes against random enemies and will be covered in more detail in a later Dev Diary. 
If you're just want to have some fun in a quick skirmish, the Battle Simulator is where to click. 

As mentioned in the trailers, I've always wanted a HUGE fantasy world to explore and travel. After playing around with different sizes, I settled on a 2500 (50 x 50) hexagonal grid.
This gives me enough room to play with and doesn't bunch everything up. It also makes the game world feel bigger and more epic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/6e936056c52eaabb6775343c3517a2ce16a4247b.png[/img]

But the problem with having a world that large is performance. The more you put on the screen, the worse performance will be. 
Many games solve this problem by limiting what's visible or being rendered at any one time. The content is restricted to one level, one town, one can only zoom so far, etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0b6b0c9925cf620d64a5bb6ae6056a196e338805.png[/img]

These optimizations I also implemented but wasn't too happy with them. I wanted the player to be able to zoom out and see the entire game world in all its glory.
I wanted to be able to put as many details on the screen without compromising on performance.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/25121adad74ade164cf7edcb202de240a391aac5.png[/img]

Previously this was not possible and the more that was rendered, the more the frame rate dropped. So with a lot of optimization, tweaking and caching, I set about improving performance.
That was the goal of the last few weeks and I think I may have achieved it. I've included some screenshots of the current look and feel of the game world. 
Don't worry, no spoilers here. This is just a draft and does not represent the final map at all. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/70dfd588e9275b0f33b87eb0ad97d1eadcf94e87.png[/img]

But I thought it important enough to share and I hope it will give potential players a better overview of what this game is about. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/a680dfa55b6f538207b6ea42b1c2cf946dcb13b7.png[/img]

I also spent some time improving the game world look. Adding things like rivers, bridges and creating a more natural looking landscape. 
Before the grid tiles looked too circular and artificial. With a little bit of adjustment, they now appear more real and natural.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/983903ac53306489ccd50ad6fd52c4cb2700e0c8.png[/img]

All that being said, the entire game world can now be rendered and I consistently reach a FPS of 110 - 120 on normal graphic settings. 
True, I am running this on a NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 but I'm hoping even older cards will be able to achieve at least 60 FPS.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/4e27f1992edb7ea61d41b096daaf08ab0988da7a.png[/img]

On a different note, I've also decided to rearrange the Chapters a bit and include three Chapters in the Early Access Game instead of two. This will expand the game play by about 10 - 20 hours.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/7deaefea66bd89ca6911d41291f87b019f8799be.png[/img]

As always, thanks for reading this far and more Dev Diaries will be coming shortly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0aac04a6424bb91c3fbbe3568c13e8c34f916c67.png[/img]

notes.title: State of the Game
notes.content:
[h2]State of the Game[/h2]

Just wanted to post an update about the current state of the game and when Early Access will be available.

The last few weeks and months I have been play testing and polishing the game. 

Somethings I am happy with, others not so much. My goal the entire time has been to create a fun game the player can escape a few hours with.

In that regard, the game is mostly successful. You begin the game with a few quests, recruit your heroes, send them out to explore, fight battles and complete quests.

For successful quests, you get rewarded and can expand. 

If you're unable to complete quests then you won't get rewarded and eventually run out of gold to recruit new heroes.

This does not necessarily mean you lose. Your heroes will slowly regain health and can still be sent on quests. You can also trade to boost your income. But there is a chance that you run out of heroes / gold and have to face the music.

So there is a bit of risk in the game and you do have to think about which quests to accept / complete and who to send on them.

So far, so good. 

But as with most games, this becomes repetitive and a bit tedious. There will be different chapters to complete which introduce new content but I'm trying to think of something bigger.

You have your private army of heroes and what else can you do with them?

I'm thinking that eventually you will have to side with one of the Factions (Human, Elven, Goblin or Undead) and wage war against the others for control of the world but this still needs to be fleshed out.

So I'm trying to keep the game engaging even in the later stages.

[h2]What's currently being worked on[/h2]

- Parts of the UI seem a little dated and I want to improve / upgrade those
- Adding more Character Skills and Spells (especially for Archer / Mage / Cleric)
- Adding more Accessories to make character customization even more unique
- Bug fixing 

[h3]Introducing deeper battles[/h3]

As you've perhaps seen from the trailers and screenshots, the battles are fought on a square-like battle board. 

This allows for some strategic variations such as structures, barriers, wave battles, etc. But it's also limited and the battles eventually become repetitive.

With this in mind, I want to expand the battles for certain locations. For example, if there is a unique location like a dungeon or tomb, this should be something bigger. There should be multiple rooms / areas that have to be explored with multiple enemies to be slayed along with an end boss.

So this is being currently worked on and will be introduced as soon as possible.


[h2]When will Early Access be available?[/h2]

This is a little difficult to say at the moment. I don't want to commit myself to a date and then not be able to deliver or deliver a shoddy product. Anyone remember Sword of the Stars II?

I want to release a polished game with enough content. Let's say a rough estimate will be the next 6 - 12 months. In the meantime, I will keep posting updates and dev diaries about new features and content.

I'm currently not active on Discord and maybe I should be. But from what I've heard, Discord is a real time-sink and at the moment I'm not able to spend that much time on it.

As always, I'll keep posting new announcements on Steam and if you have questions or comments that's where I'm the most active.

And thanks for reading to the end ːsteamhappyː

notes.title: Dev Diary #3 - The Tavern
notes.content:
[h2]The Tavern[/h2]

In each castle, town and stronghold throughout the land, the player will find a tavern filled with interesting patrons. As you travel the land and discover these locations, you'll be able to visit their taverns and interact with their guests.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/4de6c61bae69a9c0a365350df93b634b4c0e3867.png[/img]

Currently there are 5 types of patrons to find at the tavern:
[list]
[*]Quest Giver
[*]Hero for Hire
[*]Location Giver
[*]Spy
[*]Treasure Hunter
[/list]

[h3]Quest Giver[/h3]

As the name suggests, the Quest Giver will offer you quests to fulfill. These will be your primary source of income and allow you to recruit new heroes, train them, trade at the market and so on. The Quest Giver will remain at the tavern for a certain period of time and then disappear. Some quest givers will only appear at certain locations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/376125e7b602e37021f8f67cddc46d5f99008c43.png[/img]

[h3]Hero for Hire[/h3]

These heroes can be hired instead of recruited. They are experienced warriors looking for a new liege. Since they already come with skills and a certain level, the hiring cost is usually steep. After hiring, the hero can be further customized and naturally they will continue to gain in experience and level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41242435/0b39928a230f8d75fb78e1c1ed9cc199769daba2.png[/img]

[h3]Location Giver[/h3]

These patrons will offer you the location of a Point of Interest, naturally for a price. Some locations will only be discoverable through a Location Giver. Or perhaps you are simply interested in knowing where a certain location is. Furthermore, uncovering these places will trigger new quests.

[h3]Spy[/h3]

Spies are an important function of the game and the only way to gain information about what's going on in the world. For example, if Goblin Raiders or Ice Beasts have appeared and are on a rampage. Or if a location is about to attacked. It's important to have spies telling you these things.

[h3]Treasure Hunter[/h3]

There are those in this world who seek treasure but are too afraid to get it themselves. They will offer a part of it, if you find it for them. For a price, the treasure hunter will offer you a map. You will have to send a Hero Party there and deal with any opposition. If successful, you will discover the treasure and receive part of it.
